spans.text: RATIONAL NORMAL CURVES IN WEIGHTED PROJECTIVE SPACE
CAITLIN M. DAVIS AND ALEKSANDRA SOBIESKA

ABSTRACT. This article aims to extend classical homological results about the rational normal curves to analogues in weighted projective spaces. Results include determinantality and nonstandard versions of quadratic generation and the Koszul property.

This article aims to extend classical homological results about the rational normal curves to their weighted analogues. The rational normal curves provide a rich source of examples of many homological properties. In particular, the defining ideals of these curves are determinantal ([Eis05, Proposition 6.1]) with a quadratic Gröbner basis ([Stu, ERT94], [CDNR13, Theorem 3.1.1]), and their coordinate rings are Cohen-Macaulay and Koszul. We consider certain analogues of the rational normal curves in weighted projective spaces, and we show that (weighted variants of) all of these properties hold for these curves.

There has been great interest in recent years in extending homological properties to the nonstandard graded and multigraded settings, where we use nonstandard graded to refer to rings with a nonstandard

-grading. Since the generalization by Maclagan-Smith of Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity to multigraded polynomial rings ([MS04]), there have been many results on multigraded regularity: [BC17, BHS21, BHS22, CH22, CN20, SVTW06]. There has also been much work on multigraded syzygies: [BE23, BE24a, BE24b, BES20, BKLY21, BS24, BCN22, Cob24, EES15, HNVT22, HS04, HSS06, SVT06, Yan21]. In particular, the generalization of the rational normal curve studied in this article comes from Brown and Erman in [BE23].

Despite this interest in the multigraded setting, few geometric examples have been examined thoroughly. Existing work concerning geometric examples focuses primarily on sets of points: [HNVT22, SVT06]. Part of what makes the rational normal curves so important in the literature is that they can be understood from so many different perspectives. They provide an important class of examples for understanding geometric, algebraic, and homological topics, and they are useful for testing out new definitions and conjectures. Our aim is to develop an analogous class of examples that could play a similar role for the nonstandard graded setting as that theory continues to expand. With this in mind, we will not focus on the most general possible class of analogues, but rather work to build a family that can be as fully understood as the classical rational normal curves. In the study of nonstandard graded and multigraded syzygies, many classical results have multigraded analogues. However, finding these analogues can often require subtle deformations of the classical statements, techniques, or definitions. Key examples of this phenomenon can be found in [BES20], [MS04], and [BE24b].

This paper is organized as follows: In §2, we define the main object of study, the weighted rational curves. In §3, we prove that the defining ideal of each of these curves is determinantal. In §4, we establish that the generators of these ideals are in fact Gröbner bases with respect to a certain monomial order. In §5, we consider a nonstandard version of the Koszul property and show that it holds for the weighted rational curves.
